response.rationale: Several T1 meta-analyses (Spada 2010, Goo 2015, Kang 2019) show explicit instruction gives large, durable gains, but those outcomes are biased toward explicit knowledge (Doughty 2003), implicit instruction did better on delayed tests (Kang 2019), the interface debate is unresolved (talk:20 is flagged MIXED, and Paradis 2009 says explicit knowledge never converts to implicit competence), and none of the evidence directly tests whether explicit instruction predicts proficiency.
